quote.text: I hate budgeting and I've tried everything

promise.text: How to make a monthly budget for the first time

art.why: the carousel's topic: the moment and its guide name "budget"

lines.text: Take-home pay, every bill, real spending from your statements, then subtract.
A $3,240 example month, a fix for a negative number, a weekly check.

eyebrow.text: How to build yours in about an hour

body.text: Use what lands in your account after tax and deductions, not your salary.
Paid every two weeks, multiply one paycheck by 26 and divide by 12.
Paid weekly, multiply by 52 and divide by 12.

eyebrow.text: How to build yours in about an hour

head.text: List every bill with its due date.

body.text: Open last month's statements and write down rent, utilities, phone, insurance, loan payments and card minimums.

eyebrow.text: How to build yours in about an hour

head.text: Estimate the rest from real statements.

body.text: Add up groceries, fuel and eating out for each of the last two or three months and use the average, not what you think you spend.
A guess almost always runs low.

eyebrow.text: How to build yours in about an hour

head.text: Put savings and debt payments in before the extras.

items.text: Has any income come in or changed?
Has a bill changed or been paid?
Is there spending you haven't added?
Does your savings or cushion need adjusting?

line.text: This is not a budget. It is one number for what is safe to spend, with nothing to categorise and no plan to stick to.
